children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 11 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? In other words, do you live with him and/or pay for things like his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me full-time, and I'm responsible for all his care - I pay for his food, clothes, school things, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure actually - his other parent and I are separated, but I don't know if they're claiming it or not. Is that something I need to find out?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Yes, that's an important point - only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. If Alex's other parent is already claiming it, you wouldn't be able to claim it too. However, if they're not claiming it, or if you both agree that you should be the one to claim it instead, then you could proceed.

Before we determine eligibility, I have a couple more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm here in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just one more question to complete the assessment:

**Are there any special circumstances I should know about? For example, is Alex in hospital or care for extended periods, or does he work 24+ hours per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of that applies to us. Alex is just a normal 11-year-old - he goes to school, lives at home with me, and doesn't work or anything like that. He's not in hospital or care or anything.

conversation.text:
## Good news! You are **eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 11 years old (under 16)  
✓ You live with Alex in the UK  
✓ You're responsible for his care and pay for all his needs  
✓ There are no disqualifying circumstances

**Important point to be aware of:**

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. Since you mentioned you're separated from Alex's other parent and you're not sure if they're claiming:

- **If they're not currently claiming** - you can go ahead and make your claim
- **If they are claiming** - you would need to agree between yourselves who should claim. If you can't agree, HMRC will decide
- If you both want to claim and they're currently receiving it, you can contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss transferring the claim to you

**Next steps:** You can proceed with your Child Benefit claim. Just be aware that you should check whether Alex's other parent is already claiming, as this could affect when your claim can start.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
